criteria.evidence: Response explicitly says 'trace the boundary where the wrong decision happens' and lists five architectural layers (tool definitions, context, system prompt, application-layer logic, model behavior) to check before rewriting.

Response identifies tool definitions as 'most common culprit' and gives a diagnostic process (collect failure examples, look for patterns), but never commits to pinpointing a single first incorrect boundary — instead asks the user to share examples so 'I can help pinpoint which boundary is actually failing.'

Opens with 'No — replacing the framework is a disproportionate first move' and closes with 'Only escalate toward replace the framework if you've ruled out prompt/tool-definition issues AND can show an architectural limitation,' clearly discouraging unnecessary replacement.
